title: Review: SI units and prefixes; Experimental methods and practical skills; Estimation and orders of magnitude; Uncertainties and errors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS01-1#N.5, MS02-1#N.11, MS04-1#N.6, MS06-1#N.4, MS01-1#N.7, MS02-1#N.3, MS04-1#N.3, MS06-1#N.12, MS01-1#N.12, MS02-1#N.5, MS04-1#N.10, MS06-1#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Derived unit
items.clue: One obtained from a defining equation, such as m s⁻¹ for velocity.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Letter such as k, M or n placed before a symbol to stand for a power of ten.

items.label: Base units
items.clue: Building blocks such as kg, m, s, A, K and mol, from which all others are made.

items.label: Random error
items.clue: Unpredictable scatter of readings either side of the true value; reduced by repeating.

questions.stem: A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: A student measures the diameter of a wire five times with a micrometer: 0.55, 0.56, 0.55, 0.55, 0.56 mm. Later she notices that the micrometer reads 0.03 mm when fully closed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The readings are accurate, because they agree closely with each other.
Taking more readings and averaging them would remove the error.
The readings are precise but not accurate; subtract 0.03 mm from each.
The error is random, so a micrometer with a finer resolution is needed.

questions.explanation: Small spread means precise. The zero error is systematic: correct it by subtracting the zero reading, giving about 0.52–0.53 mm.

questions.stem: What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: On a pair of vernier callipers, the vernier's zero lies between the 31 mm and 32 mm marks of the main scale. Vernier mark 6 lines up exactly with a main-scale mark. What is the reading?
questions.explanation: Main scale up to the vernier's zero: 31 mm. Vernier mark 6 lines up: 6 × 0.1 mm = 0.6 mm. Reading = 31.6 mm.

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?

A student times a trolley rolling down a ramp with a hand-held stopwatch that reads to 0.01 s. Her five times vary by about 0.2 s. Which change would most reduce the effect of this random error on her result?

options.text: Use a stopwatch that reads to 0.001 s instead of 0.01 s.
Check that the stopwatch reads zero before each timing.
Subtract her typical reaction time from each reading.
Time the run with light gates and an electronic timer.

questions.explanation: The varying human reaction is the source of the scatter. Automatic timing removes it.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: A student investigates how the time t for a ball to fall from rest depends on the drop height h. (h = ½gt², with g constant.) Which plan is best?

options.text: Drop the ball once from each of three heights, timing by hand; plot t against h.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t².
Drop a ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically, with a heavier ball for the greater heights.

questions.explanation: Enough values, repeats, no reaction time, and h = (g/2)t² gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2.

questions.stem: Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.stem: A ball's fall is timed four times: 0.62 s, 0.57 s, 0.65 s, 0.60 s. The stopwatch reads to 0.01 s. Which is the best way to write the result?
questions.explanation: Mean = 2.44 ÷ 4 = 0.61 s. Half the range = (0.65 − 0.57) ÷ 2 = 0.04 s. The scatter is far bigger than the resolution, so it sets the uncertainty.

questions.stem: A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: One complete cycle of a wave on an oscilloscope screen spans 2.5 divisions. The time-base is set to 2.0 ms div⁻¹. What is the frequency of the signal?
